column10: getAppDataFileByName merges _fileId and _file into the returned data object. If a caller passes this result directly to updateFileContent, those metadata properties will be written back into the stored JSON file content, silently corrupting it. The file metadata should be returned separately (e.g. as a wrapper object), not spread into T.

folderId is interpolated directly into the Drive query string without escaping: `'${folderId}' in parents`. All other user-controlled string values go through escapeDriveQueryValue, but folderId is skipped. A malformed or attacker-controlled folderId containing `'` or `\` could inject additional query clauses and return unexpected files.

The multipart boundary is generated with Date.now(), giving a value like 'drive_boundary_1715000000000'. If JSON.stringify(data) or JSON.stringify(metadata) happens to contain this exact string (e.g. a value stored in a previous file that was loaded back), the multipart body will be structurally corrupted because the parser will treat the embedded string as a boundary delimiter. RFC 2046 requires boundaries to be chosen to not appear in the body; crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.getRandomValues() should be used instead.

uploadImage also uses Date.now() for the boundary with the same collision risk as buildMultipartBody. For binary image content, the chance of the boundary string occurring in the blob is low but non-zero; use crypto.randomUUID() to eliminate the risk.

apiFetch returns `undefined as T` for 204 responses. All callers are typed to receive a concrete type (e.g. DriveFile), so they silently receive undefined without TypeScript catching it. deleteFile avoids this by using apiFetchRaw, but any future method that causes a 204 via apiFetch will have undefined returned where a value is expected. The overload should be separated or the 204 case made explicit in the return type.

getAppDataFileByName has no orderBy clause, so when multiple files share the same name in appDataFolder (which createAppDataFile allows, since it does no deduplication check), the returned file is non-deterministic. Combined with the lack of a duplicate-creation guard, repeated calls to createAppDataFile with the same name accumulate stale copies and the retrieved file is arbitrary.

findOrCreateFolder has a TOCTOU race: two concurrent calls (e.g. two browser tabs sharing the same access token) both see no existing folder, then both call createFolder, producing two folders with the same name. The Drive API's drive.file scope means both tabs can see and further corrupt each other's folder references. The Drive API has no atomic find-or-create primitive, but callers should be made aware that deduplication cannot be guaranteed, or the method should return an array / accept a known parent scope to reduce the window.

createAppDataFile (and updateFileContent at line 238) bypass the buildHeaders / apiFetch helpers and call fetch directly with a manually constructed Authorization header. If the token management logic in buildHeaders ever changes (e.g. adding required headers), these paths will silently skip them. These upload paths should be refactored to use authFetch or a shared upload helper.

buildMultipartBody always sets 'Content-Type: application/json' for both the metadata and content parts. The data parameter is typed as unknown, so callers could theoretically pass non-JSON-serialisable values; JSON.stringify(data) would then produce 'null' or throw, silently losing data. The function should constrain data to a JSON-safe type (or document the JSON-only contract) to prevent silent data loss at the call site.

listAppDataFiles uses only 'trashed = false' as the query filter with spaces=appDataFolder. Unlike getAppDataFileByName it does not include "'appDataFolder' in parents", which means if the Drive API ever returns files from nested paths within that space, all of them are included without the caller being able to distinguish hierarchy. This is an inconsistency with getAppDataFileByName and may silently return unexpected files as the stored data grows.
`updateFileMetadata`の引数`patch`の型定義`{ name?: string; addParents?: string; removeParents?: string }`がインラインで定義されています。この型は他の場所で再利用される可能性があり、また可読性の観点からも、ファイル上部で`type`エイリアスとして定義することが望ましいです。
`listFilesInFolder`メソッドは、ページネーションのために`nextPageToken`を使用していますが、変数名が`pageToken`となっています。`nextPageToken`という変数名は`listAppDataFiles`メソッドでは正しく使われており、一貫性を保つためにも`nextPageToken`に修正することが望ましいです。
`DriveFile`型は、このファイル内でDrive APIレスポンスの一部として複数回利用されています。一方で、将来的にはアプリケーションのドメインモデルとして`DriveFile`とは異なる構造の型が定義される可能性があります。この型がAPIクライアントの内部的なデータ転送オブジェクト（DTO）であることを明確にするため、`DriveFileDTO`のような名前に変更することを推奨します。

The buildHeaders method defaults to setting 'Content-Type' to 'application/json' if the body is present. This might incorrectly override non-JSON content types. Explicitly check and respect the content type of the init.headers or the request body.

The uploadImage method creates a full Blob for the multipart request but does not handle potential memory overhead for large files. Consider streaming the file contents instead of building the entire payload in memory.
The updateFileContent method assumes the body content is JSON during the call to buildMultipartBody. Handling non-JSON data types uniformly with the buildHeaders logic would make the API more robust.
The listAppDataFiles method uses pageSize=100 but does not allow overriding this value. Exporting this parameter for caller configuration can improve flexibility and control.

The updateFileMetadata method allows free-form metadata updates but does not validate or sanitize the inputs. Validating input structure and preventing unexpected API payload failures would improve stability.

The DriveQuotaExceededError class conflates status codes 429 and 403 for rate-limiting scenarios, which might obscure distinguishing between quota and general permission errors. Clarify or split handling for better granularity.

The findFolderByName method sorts by name but does not handle cases with multiple matches. Returning the most recently modified or another prioritized match instead of the name order might improve precision.
The getDownloadUrl method assumes webContentLink availability for downloadable files directly. Some file types might require additional API calls to generate links. Add handling for such cases.

`findFolderByName` searches `spaces=drive` for any folder matching the name. With the OAuth scopes currently requested in `auth-context.tsx` (`drive.file` + `drive.appdata`), the app can only see folders it has itself created/opened, which means this method silently returns `null` for folders the user created via the Drive UI. If that is intended behavior it should be documented in the JSDoc, otherwise callers may be surprised that `findOrCreateFolder` creates duplicate folders alongside user‑owned ones with the same name.

`getDownloadUrl` relies on `webContentLink`, which Drive only returns for files that are publicly/anyone-with-link shared. For files uploaded via `uploadImage` to a private folder (the typical case for this app), the API will return no `webContentLink` and this method will return `null`, even though the file exists and is accessible. The JSDoc says "非バイナリ等で取得不可" but that is misleading — the real condition is the file's sharing state. Consider clarifying the doc, or switching to constructing an authenticated `?alt=media` URL (or returning a Blob URL via `getFileBlob`).

`findFolderByName` is documented and paired with `createFolder` as operating on the My Drive root, but the query does not constrain the parent to `root`. Drive searches the whole `drive` space here, so `findOrCreateFolder` can return an unrelated same-named folder from a nested/shared location and subsequent uploads will go to the wrong folder. Add a parent constraint (for example the root folder, or an explicit parent parameter) to make lookup match creation.
